children: Nippon India Mutual Fund acquired 12.94 lakh Escorts Kubota shares, representing a 1.16 per cent stake, for Rs 361.69 crore
HDFC Mutual Fund (MF) sold a 1.45 per cent stake in agriculture and engineering company Escorts Kubota for Rs 453 crore through a bulk deal on the BSE on Wednesday.

According to exchange data, HDFC MF offloaded 16.21 lakh shares of the Faridabad-based company at an average price of Rs 2,794 per share. Following the transaction, HDFC MF’s holding in Escorts Kubota through its schemes declined to 5.49 per cent from 6.94 per cent.

Nippon India Mutual Fund acquired 12.94 lakh shares, representing a 1.16 per cent stake, at the same price. The transaction was valued at Rs 361.69 crore. Details of other buyers could not be ascertained.
Escorts Kubota shares rose nearly 1 per cent on Thursday to trade at Rs 2,820.75 apiece on the BSE.

In a separate bulk deal on the BSE, Business Excellence Trust III, a Sebi-registered alternative investment fund managed by Motilal Oswal Alternates, sold 29.96 lakh shares of Molbio Diagnostics, representing a 2.6 per cent stake, for Rs 394 crore.
The shares were sold at an average price of Rs 1,315 apiece. Despite the transaction, Business Excellence Trust III remained the largest public shareholder in Goa-based Molbio Diagnostics.
Kotak Mahindra MF acquired 27.50 lakh shares, representing nearly a 2.4 per cent stake, for more than Rs 361 crore. Details of other buyers could not be ascertained.
Molbio Diagnostics shares declined 3.39 per cent on Thursday to trade at Rs 1,266 apiece on the BSE.
